questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to improve my Spanish, so selecting a Spanish-speaking country was essential.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy, they provided us with an email with all the necessary information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus coordinator was very helpful in guiding us when we had difficulties. They also organized a welcome event for the Erasmus students where they explained all the necessary information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy. We were three people going from Denmark, so we used the website "Spotahome".

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You might not get the typical "Erasmus experience" when living off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had an Erasmus coordinator, Oscar, who was very helpful. I changed courses several times before getting completely settled, and he was very helpful throughout these processes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As explained above.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up being very satisfied with my courses. The teachers were very helpful as well in providing information about the courses, like which teachers are more accustomed to exchange students, and which courses might be too difficult etc.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask the teachers and Erasmus coordinator for help, they are very helpfull!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I believe the workload is higher in Barcelona than in Denmark. The courses are only graded at 6 ECTS, which I don't think is fitting. This might also be due to the fact that I surely don't speak Spanish as well as the natives.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It depended a lot on the courses and the teacher, some of them were very similar to the ones in Denmark, others weren't. Some of them were more like a "lecture", in others the students were more included.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Linguistics
Sociolingüística del español
El cine y la industria cultural
El Procés de Producció Audiovisual
Ensenyament de l'Anglès com a Llengua Estrangera

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend "Sociolingüística del español." This course is very exciting if you are interested in the Spanish-speaking world and the differences between various dialects. The teacher is very engaged and inclusive. She paid a lot of attention to the exchange students and wanted to hear our thoughts and opinions.
Additionally, the course "El Procés de Producció Audiovisual" was very different and exciting! Not many exchange students choose this subject, and you get paired in groups for a short film project. This provided a great opportunity to make Catalan friends and speak Spanish more.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My personal spending was a lot higher than in Denmark because of all the different things I wanted to experience. This included various activities, tips, and visiting different Spanish cities etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating in restaurants and buying groceries were significant expenses. The drinks were very cheap, but the food at restaurants was more or less at Danish prices, only a bit cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything! You can do whatever sport or activity you like. The app "Meetup" is very good for all sorts of events and activities, including free ones.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Dancing! There is a huge dancing environment in Barcelona, especially for salsa and bachata.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would definitely visit the different cities close to Barcelona, like Costa Brava. Also Valencia is only 3,5 hours away in bus, which is great for a weekend trip.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not as much as I expected. Barcelona is an international city, with 20-30% of the population in the city center being foreigners. However, choosing subjects at the university that were not common for exchange students and getting paired in groups helped me a lot!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It's a bit hard to get into the local environment as an exchange student if you don't speak the language perfectly, especially since many prefer speaking in Catalan.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: My experience was that they are very spontaneous. They eat dinner very late, so the city is always full of life and people until very late at night.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make sure to get Spanish-speaking roommates. I lived with two people from Denmark, which hindered my improvement in speaking Spanish a lot! Prioritize an apartment close to or in the city center; it is definitely worth the extra money. 
Investigate different courses and ask the teachers or Erasmus coordinator for help.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of right now..

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in a different city and experiencing its culture is a completely different experience compared to being a tourist.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting out of my comfort zone and speaking Spanish as much as possible without worrying about the mistakes I might make.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
